subject: TTFT / streaming requirements — follow-up and pilot action items
messages:
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
To: Emma Stone <emma.stone@edgecart.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 30 Apr 2027 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: TTFT / streaming requirements — follow-up and pilot action items

Thanks again for the call today, Emma — really helpful to see EdgeCart's interactive checkout flow and the latency constraints you outlined. Below is a concise recap and proposed next steps so we can scope a short pilot.

Quick recap of requirements (as discussed):
- Target TTFT: P95 <= 150 ms for short prompts (user prompts + few-shot context) under normal traffic; goal P50 ~ 80-100 ms.
- Sustained throughput: nominal 50 QPS, peak bursts up to 200 QPS for promo spikes.
- Concurrency: ~20 active streaming sessions per instance; want linear scaling across nodes.
- Streaming: prefer SSE to simplify browser consumption; must support WebSocket fallback for older clients. Chunk cadence: small incremental chunks, ideally every 200-400ms for UI smoothness.
- Model: ~7B quantized variant (you mentioned latency-first profile).
- Compliance: SOC 2 required; private logs for audit.

Attachments: initial TTFT/streaming SLO proposal (PDF) and a sample prompt set (JSON).

Proposed next steps (owners):
1) Ben: scope perf pilot (runbook + cost estimate) and propose server config (GPU type, batching, cache hints). Target by Mon, 3 May.
2) Monica: gather SOC 2 evidence and share checklist; also capture expected data retention window.
3) EdgeCart (Emma + SRE): share a small representative traffic trace and the sample prompt set (we can use the attached JSON format).
4) Schedule: aim to run a 48-72 hour pilot the week of 10 May if we have data and access.

A few technical notes from the call I want to capture for the pilot scope:
- Prioritize low-latency execution path: small batch sizes, KV caching for repeated user system prompts, and prefix caching for session tokens.
- If SSE P95 doesn't meet 150ms, we'll try a WebSocket + aggressive prefetch of first token (packet priming) as fallback.
- Chunk sizing: we recommend chunk boundaries roughly every 200–400ms vs token-count thresholds so UI feels live; we'll instrument for chunk size vs perceived latency.

Please reply if anything above is off. Emma — if you can drop a 1–2 minute example trace (HTTP timestamps or a HAR), that will let Ben size our estimate quickly.

Thanks,

Evelyn Hart
Enterprise Lead, EMEA
Redwood Inference
(Attachment: 2027-04-30_Redwood-TTFT-proposal.pdf)
(Attachment: edgecart_sample_prompts.json)

From: Emma Stone <emma.stone@edgecart.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
Cc: EdgeCart SRE <sre@edgecart.com>
Date: Mon, 3 May 2027 09:03:00 +0100
Subject: Re: TTFT / streaming requirements — follow-up and pilot action items

Thanks, Evelyn — this aligns with what we need. A couple clarifications from the SRE side:
- The 150 ms P95 is firm for the checkout microflow; we've seen user drop-off when RTTs exceed that. If you can show a credible plan to meet P95=150 under 50 QPS nominal and 200 QPS bursts, we're happy to proceed.
- Region: primary EU (Frankfurt) for data residency.
- Model details: we'll use your 7B quantized profile if you recommend it; our baseline test uses ~1.5 KB average prompt size (mostly user utterances + product context).
- Security: SOC 2 in place, but we need a tighter retention policy for session logs (30 days default). Monica — can you advise?

I've attached a short HAR and a synthetic traffic sample for the checkout flow. We'll share creds for a staging endpoint when ready.

Emma
Head of Product
EdgeCart
(Attachment: edgecart_checkout_trace.har)

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>, Emma Stone <emma.stone@edgecart.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 3 May 2027 12:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: TTFT / streaming requirements — follow-up and pilot action items

Great notes — here's a short technical addendum to make the pilot concrete and unblock cost sizing.

Pilot plan (technical):
- Infra: start with 2 x A10G-equivalent nodes in eu-central for the pilot (can scale to 4 for burst window). We'll colocate model + serving runtime.
- Serving config: single-model endpoint with low-latency profile: batch size cap 8, dynamic batching disabled for first-token path, KV cache enabled for session prefixes.
- Streaming: SSE primary; we will enable a WebSocket endpoint for clients that prefer binary frames. We'll instrument both.
- Chunk cadence: server will emit partial chunks every 250ms target; chunk size heuristic will aim for small deltas (~32–128 tokens max) to keep perceived latency low.
- Throughput: with the above profile we expect median TTFT ~60–110ms for the 7B quantized model at 50 QPS; P95 depends on prompt length and tail spikes — pilot will determine exact P95 under your trace.

Data / access we need from EdgeCart:
- Representative traffic (thanks for the HAR) + a 24 hr sample of peak-minute traffic if possible.
- A small set of golden prompts (10–20) to use for evals.

Next steps (owners & dates):
- Ben: deliver pilot runbook + cost estimate by Tue, 4 May (end of day).
- Monica: confirm SOC2 evidence & retention options by Wed, 5 May.
- Laura: set up the pilot calendar and shared runbook link.

If EdgeCart is okay with the infra assumptions above I'll put together the provisioning steps and a quick test harness (SSE + WS) you can hit from staging.

— Ben
Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>

I've uploaded the pilot runbook template and the sample prompt tracker to the Drive folder (link above). Laura — please schedule a 1-hour kickoff for Wed, 5 May (E/T morning / EU afternoon) to align the pilot instrumentation and to review the HAR trace Emma sent.
